knowledge:
- key_parameters: hlaSetKernelTarget=Selects target CPU intrinsics (e.g., "sse4", "avx", "avx2", "avx512f", "avx512bw", "max", "auto.avx2") to optimize algorithm efficiency ;; nclassifier=The number of individual classifiers to build in the ensemble (typically 100) ;; cl=The number of threads or a cluster object for parallel computing ;; type=The type of prediction output, such as "response+prob" to return both best-guess genotypes and posterior probabilities ;; model=The genetic model used in association tests ("dominant", "additive", "recessive", "genotype") ;; prob.threshold=The posterior probability threshold below which imputed genotypes are excluded from association testing ;; rm.unused.snp=Logical indicating whether to remove unused SNPs from the model object before publishing ;; anonymize=Logical indicating whether to remove individual training genotypes and sample IDs to protect confidentiality
- alternatives: Sequence-based typing (SBT) is mentioned as the gold standard for classical HLA genotyping, but it is noted as time-consuming and cost-prohibitive compared to HIBAG's imputation approach.
- when_to_use: Use HIBAG when you have GWAS SNP data (specifically flanking the MHC region on chromosome 6) and want to impute classical HLA alleles (e.g., HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1) either using pre-fit published models or by training a custom model on a reference panel.
- pitfalls: AVX512 CPU throttling can occur when using AVX512 intrinsics, so hlaSetKernelTarget("auto.avx2") is recommended if throttling is observed ;; A very low matching proportion indicates that the test SNP profile is underrepresented in the training set, which may affect imputation reliability ;; Array-based platforms may have ambiguous strands, requiring careful matching of SNPs between the model and test data ;; Releasing raw trained models can leak confidential individual genotypes; always use hlaPublish with anonymize=TRUE to strip sensitive training data.

workflows.name: hla_imputation_prefit
workflows.intent: Impute classical HLA alleles from user-provided PLINK SNP data using pre-fit published HIBAG models.
workflows.stages: 1. Load the pre-fit model list and extract the model for the target HLA locus ;; 2. Import the user's PLINK BED files into HIBAG genotype format ;; 3. Predict HLA genotypes and posterior probabilities using the model
workflows.code:
filename <- system.file ( "extdata" , "ModelList.RData" , package= "HIBAG" )
model.list <- get ( load (filename))
hla.id <- "A"
model <- hlaModelFromObj (model.list[[hla.id]])
summary (model)
plot (model)
head (model $ snp.id)
head (model $ snp.position)
yourgeno <- hlaBED2Geno ( bed.fn= ".bed" , fam.fn= ".fam" , bim.fn= ".bim" )
summary (yourgeno)
pred.guess <- hlaPredict (model, yourgeno, type= "response+prob" )
summary (pred.guess)
pred.guess $ value
pred.guess $ postprob

workflows.name: custom_model_training_validation
workflows.intent: Train a custom HIBAG model using a reference panel of known HLA and SNP genotypes, validate its accuracy, and export a clean model for release.
workflows.stages: 1. Format reference HLA alleles ;; 2. Define flanking SNP regions and subset genotypes ;; 3. Split reference data into training and validation sets ;; 4. Train the HIBAG model (sequentially or in parallel) ;; 5. Predict HLA alleles on validation data ;; 6. Evaluate accuracy and generate diagnostic plots/reports ;; 7. Publish and anonymize the model for public release
workflows.code:
hla.id <- "A"
train.HLA <- hlaAllele (HLA_Type_Table $ sample.id, H1 = HLA_Type_Table[, paste (hla.id, ".1" , sep= "" )], H2 = HLA_Type_Table[, paste (hla.id, ".2" , sep= "" )], locus= hla.id, assembly= "hg19" )
region <- 500
train.geno <- hlaGenoSubsetFlank (HapMap_CEU_Geno, hla.id, region * 1000 , assembly= "hg19" )
summary (train.geno)
set.seed ( 100 )
model <- hlaAttrBagging (train.HLA, train.geno, nclassifier= 100 )
summary (model)
cl <- 2
set.seed ( 1000 )
hlaParallelAttrBagging (cl, train.HLA, train.geno, nclassifier= 100 , auto.save= "AutoSaveModel.RData" )
model.obj <- get ( load ( "AutoSaveModel.RData" ))
model <- hlaModelFromObj (model.obj)
summary (model)
pred.guess <- hlaPredict (model, yourgeno, type= "response+prob" , cl= cl)
hlatab <- hlaSplitAllele (hla, train.prop= 0.5 )
snpid <- hlaFlankingSNP (HapMap_CEU_Geno $ snp.id, HapMap_CEU_Geno $ snp.position, hla.id, region * 1000 , assembly= "hg19" )
train.geno <- hlaGenoSubset (HapMap_CEU_Geno, snp.sel = match (snpid, HapMap_CEU_Geno $ snp.id), samp.sel = match (hlatab $ training $ value $ sample.id, HapMap_CEU_Geno $ sample.id))
test.geno <- hlaGenoSubset (HapMap_CEU_Geno, samp.sel= match ( hlatab $ validation $ value $ sample.id, HapMap_CEU_Geno $ sample.id))
model <- hlaAttrBagging (hlatab $ training, train.geno, nclassifier= 100 )
pred <- hlaPredict (model, test.geno)
comp <- hlaCompareAllele (hlatab $ validation, pred, allele.limit= model, call.threshold= 0 )
comp $ overall
d <- hlaDistance (model)
p <- hclust ( as.dist (d))
plot (p, xlab= "HLA alleles" )
hlaReportPlot (pred, model= model, fig= "matching" )
hlaReportPlot (pred, hlatab $ validation, fig= "call.rate" )
hlaReportPlot (pred, hlatab $ validation, fig= "call.threshold" )
hlaReport (comp, type= "txt" )
hlaReport (comp, type= "markdown" )
hlaReport (comp, type= "tex" , header= FALSE )
mobj <- hlaPublish (model, platform = "Illumina 1M Duo" , information = "Training set -- HapMap Phase II" , warning = NULL , rm.unused.snp= TRUE , anonymize= TRUE )
save (mobj, file= "Your_HIBAG_Model.RData" )

workflows.name: hla_association_testing
workflows.intent: Perform association tests between imputed HLA alleles (or translated amino acid sequences) and clinical phenotypes.
input: Imputed HLA genotypes (from hlaPredict or hlaAllele)
workflows.stages: 1. Load phenotype and covariate data ;; 2. Format HLA alleles into a HIBAG allele object ;; 3. Run association tests using dominant, additive, or recessive models ;; 4. Convert HLA alleles to amino acid sequences ;; 5. Run amino acid-level association tests
workflows.code:
dat <- read.table (fn, header= TRUE , stringsAsFactors= FALSE )
head (dat)
hla <- hlaAllele (dat $ sample.id, H1= dat $ A, H2= dat $ A .1 , locus= "A" , assembly= "hg19" , prob= dat $ prob)
summary (hla)
hlaAssocTest (hla, disease ~ h, data= dat)
print ( hlaAssocTest (hla, disease ~ h, data= dat, verbose= FALSE ))
hlaAssocTest (hla, disease ~ h, data= dat, prob.threshold= 0.5 )
hlaAssocTest (hla, disease ~ h, data= dat, showOR= TRUE )
hlaAssocTest (hla, disease ~ h, data= dat, model= "additive" )
hlaAssocTest (hla, trait ~ h, data= dat)
aa <- hlaConvSequence (hla, code= "P.code.merge" )
head ( c (aa $ value $ allele1, aa $ value $ allele2))
summary (aa)
hlaAssocTest (aa, disease ~ h, data= dat, model= "dominant" )
hlaAssocTest (aa, disease ~ h, data= dat, model= "dominant" , prob.threshold= 0.5 )
hlaAssocTest (aa, disease ~ h, data= dat, model= "recessive" )
